args.summary: Deployed hotfix v2.3.2 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to remediate elevated error rate on v2.3.1. Pre-deploy state: v2.3.1 deployed everywhere, unhealthy, error rate 18%. Deploy required change-manager approval because v2.3.2 had never been healthy in production; approval was granted and the rollout verified. Post-deploy state: all three regions on v2.3.2, healthy, error rate 0.2%. No rollback performed. Change record only — service is currently healthy.
args.title: checkout-api hotfix v2.3.2 deployed to production to resolve v2.3.1 elevated error rate

trace.final:
Both tasks are done.

**What I did:**

1. **Assessed before acting** — checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions, marked unhealthy with an 18% error rate. The hotfix v2.3.2 had never been released to production (only v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 were previously healthy).

2. **Deployed v2.3.2** — Because v2.3.2 had never been healthy in production, this triggered the change-manager approval requirement. The deploy routed for approval, was approved, and rolled out to us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

**Verified post-deploy** — all three regions on v2.3.2, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2% (from 18%).

3. **Opened incident INC-0001** (SEV3, checkout-api) recording the change.

**Worth flagging:** The incident is a SEV3 change record, as you asked, but it paged the on-call engineer — SEV3 pages aren't usually warranted for a change that landed cleanly. If you wanted this purely as a paper trail rather than a page, that's worth noting; you may want to close it quickly or adjust the severity. Also, v2.3.1 remains flagged unhealthy in the release history and the v2.3.1-rc staging build was likewise unhealthy — the underlying cause of the regression isn't investigated here, and the hotfix is a roll-forward rather than a rollback. If v2.3.2 turns out to have masked rather than fixed the bug, that history is worth reviewing.
